prompt_text: Train a classifier on the data in this directory (README.md describes it) and report its held-out performance. Python (numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn) is available; create scripts with the Write tool.
answer:
I trained a logistic regression on `coexpression_z`, the only feature in the data. Its held-out AUROC on the 120 test pairs is **0.652**.

- **Data:** There are 480 training pairs and 120 test pairs. About 17% of pairs are positive in both sets.
- **Model:** I used a plain logistic regression with default settings and did no tuning. I only trained it on the training pairs and scored it once on the test pairs.
- **Protein overlap:** The train and test splits share proteins. All 59 proteins in the test set also appear in training, and every test pair has both of its proteins seen in training. No exact pair appears in both sets.
- **Why I didn't use protein IDs:** A model using protein identity, such as per-protein interaction rates, would probably score higher on this split. That gain would come from proteins that interact often (hubs) rather than from the pair itself, so it would overstate how well the model works on new proteins. I left those features out.
- **Test-set size:** With only about 20 positive test pairs, the AUROC estimate is noisy. Treat 0.65 as a rough figure, not a precise one.

The script is `run.py` in the working directory.

cd /tmp/review-gcn6ejga/analysis && cat > run.py <<'E'
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
tr=pd.read_csv('pairs_train.csv');te=pd.read_csv('pairs_test.csv')
print(tr.label.mean(),te.label.mean())
ptr=set(tr.protein_a)|set(tr.protein_b);pte=set(te.protein_a)|set(te.protein_b)
print(len(ptr),len(pte),len(ptr&pte))
print('test pairs with both proteins seen:',te.apply(lambda r:r.protein_a in ptr and r.protein_b in ptr,axis=1).mean())
print('dup pairs',len(set(map(frozenset,zip(tr.protein_a,tr.protein_b)))&set(map(frozenset,zip(te.protein_a,te.protein_b)))))
f=['coexpression_z']
m=LogisticRegression().fit(tr[f],tr.label);print('LR coexp AUROC',roc_auc_score(te.label,m.predict_proba(te[f])[:,1]))
E
python run.py
